title: The Brown Ring Test: qualitative test for nitrate ions

provenance.source: Reference video supplied by the channel owner (downloaded from Facebook, 720x1280).
provenance.method: 24 frames sampled evenly plus full-size stills; scene timing is accurate to about 1 s.
provenance.audio_finding: Music only: speech recognition found no speech.
provenance.reuse: Use as a style and structure reference. Change the brand, wording and data; do not republish it as is.

builder_instructions: Recreate a 20 s vertical 3D lab animation in one continuous shot. A test tube in a rack is filled in two layers, a brown ring forms at the junction, and a ball-and-stick model of the complex appears. All teaching is on-screen text: a fixed header with a step pill, labels with leader lines, and one bottom card per step holding a heading, one equation and one supporting line. No narration.

intent.goal: Show the four steps of the brown ring test and the chemistry behind the ring.
intent.audience: Secondary and first-year university chemistry students.
intent.takeaway: Nitrate is reduced to NO at the acid junction; NO binds iron(II) and gives the brown ring.
intent.hook: A glowing ring appears between two clear liquids.

style.mood: calm, precise, slightly dramatic lab at night

equations.colour: white with teal and amber species

materials.glass: thin clear glass, bright Fresnel edges, soft vertical highlight
materials.rack: matte rust-orange block with round holes

lighting.glow: additive orange at the ring with small white sparkles

style.background: plain dark navy wall, dark blue bench with a visible horizon line
style.motion_language: slow eased camera moves, fades of 0.3 to 0.5 s, nothing bounces
style.transitions: cross-fades between step cards; no cuts

wordmark.fill: animated rainbow gradient (pink, amber, green, blue, violet)

layout.note: The card reaches the bottom 5% of the frame, where Reels and Shorts draw their own controls. Our layouts keep text above the bottom 16%.

moves.shot: medium: tube, rack and two bottles
close on the junction of the two layers
medium, tube moved right, molecule at left

objects.note: tall, in the rack, slightly right of centre
enters from the top right, tip against the tube wall

objects.atoms: Fe orange centre, five water O red with white H, NO on the axis (N blue, O red, yellow bond)

equations.verified_here: atoms and charge (+9 each side) balance

weak_points_in_the_original: The 'Yield' bar (26% to 93%) and 'Fe²⁺ mix' percentage are animation progress, not measured quantities. Our ledger refuses numbers like these unless they are labelled as animation progress or computed.
The line y(τ) = y₀ − 0.5 g τ² is decoration next to a chemistry step.

timeline.visual: Pale teal liquid rises in the tube to about one third while the pipette rests on the rim.

card.heading: 1. Add Freshly Prepared FeSO₄ to Aqueous NO₃⁻ Sample
card.footer: y(τ) = y₀ − 0.5 g τ²   Fe²⁺ mix: 0% → 100%

timeline.visual: Acid runs down the wall; a clear dense layer grows under the teal layer, lifting it.

card.heading: 2. Pour Dense Conc. H₂SO₄ Slowly Down Tube Wall (ρ = 1.84 g/cm³)
card.footer: Dense H₂SO₄ sinks below the aqueous layer without mixing

timeline.visual: Push in. An orange-brown glowing band with white sparkles forms at the junction.

card.heading: 3. Interfacial Coordination Forms the Brown Ring Complex

timeline.visual: Pull back. The ball-and-stick complex flies in at the left and turns slowly; a thin gold halo circles it once.

avoid: more than one equation per card
qa_checklist: Every equation balances for atoms and charge.
Layers stay in density order: acid below the aqueous layer.
The ring sits exactly at the junction.
Text is readable at 360 px width.
